open_points.subject: secure component-by-component path opening
open_points.text: “The data directory itself is reached as A17 rule 1 reaches the configuration file, component by component with `O_NOFOLLOW`” conflicts with “modules on one line do not know each other”; `store` and `installation` are on the same line, while their sections respectively hide “opening without following links” and “the configuration format, the file-mode checks, the credential reference resolution on the host.”
open_points.question: Which module owns the shared component-by-component path-opening mechanism, and how may both `installation` and `store` use it without duplicating ownership or violating the dependency order?
options: `installation` owns it and `store` may depend on `installation`
`store` and `installation` independently implement and own their respective copies
a lower shared module owns the mechanism and both modules depend on it
open_points.default_guess: Introduce a lower shared mechanism owned by neither `installation` nor `store`, with both depending on it.

open_points.subject: Linux-only runtime and facility assumptions in A20 rule 3
open_points.text: A20 rule 3 now says “A release runs on Linux and on no other host” and “the kernel neither tests the host nor defines what it does on an unsupported one,” while State 3 says “a rule this text places outside the running kernel (A20 rule 3, A21), which no module owns” and later limits A20 rule 3 to “The pinned Python dependencies and sandbox runtime.”
open_points.question: Who owns the newly added Linux-only constraint and the requirement that runtime code use Linux facilities without availability checks?
options: the release build owns all of A20 rule 3, including platform targeting and verification
each runtime module owns unconditional use of the Linux facilities it needs
`data_provider` owns the host/facility policy consumed by runtime modules
open_points.default_guess: The release build owns Linux platform targeting, while each facility-using runtime module owns its unconditional Linux call; State 3 must state that split.

open_points.subject: unsupported Linux facility handling versus sandbox start probe
open_points.text: A20 rule 3 says “A Linux that lacks a facility these rules use — `O_PATH`, `O_NOFOLLOW`, the namespaces and limits of A03 — is unsupported as another system is: the kernel neither tests the host nor defines what it does on an unsupported one.” A03 rule 8 says “The kernel checks at start ... that one probe execution succeeds; without both it does not start, and says why,” and State 3 assigns `sandbox.probe_sandbox` that start probe.
open_points.question: When Linux lacks a namespace or limit required by A03, is the mandated probe supposed to detect the failure and produce the defined start refusal, or is behavior genuinely undefined as A20 now says?
options: the probe still runs and failure produces A03's defined start refusal
the kernel performs no probe on such an unsupported host and behavior is undefined
A20 forbids only a separate compatibility/version probe, while A03's operational probe remains required
open_points.default_guess: Treat A20 as forbidding a separate compatibility probe; retain A03's operational probe and its defined start refusal.
